chapter: Tick Chambers and the Dodds brothers
title: The Dodds brothers' deaths in Chicago
summary: Baby Dodds's recent death, his last illness, Johnny's son in New Orleans, and the Dodds siblings who died.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: You knew that Baby died a month ago.

Yeah, I didn't know it until we had to pick up a magazine over there and they had it in his magazine that he had to pass. And the people over there, you know, it was kind of shocked to them. Yeah, of course he'd been so sick since September.

Because they had been asking me about it and I told them that he was a little sick because the time that you told me you had went up there. Yeah. Yeah, well after my father's death when I went up there, he was sick but he was at home, you know.
Yeah, he'd been in the hospital.
Yeah, he'd been in the hospital, yeah. So I told him, I said, well Baby was very little sick. I said, I don't think he's going to make it. Well Johnny, Johnny's got a son here.
Well that's right, I haven't seen him since I've been there.
Rudolph, I think. Yeah, well he drives a cab on the Morrison cab line. Then he's got a nephew there which is... Oh Lawrence Dent, I know him.
Lawrence Dent, yeah. I know him, I see him, he plays in one of the bands, the Gibson band. Is that good clarinet now?

Yeah, that's what Lawrence said. So I told Lawrence, Christmas evening, the night I was leaving, he brought me here. He brought me home because I had to get ready to go to the station. And I told him about Baby being sick and he said that he was thinking he was going to go to Chicago. I said, well he's very little sick. I said, now I wrote him a card and I got an answer from him. I said, but he's very, very little. And so I said, he said, well I'm going to drive up there and see about him. Now I don't know if he went. You see, and after I got... Yeah, so I wrote to him from England and somebody answered the letter, you know, he was very bad off. He was expecting him and so when I pick up this magazine he had them passed. All three of them, all three of the brothers died in Chicago.
The Baby lived longer to be older than any of them and also older than any of his sisters too.
That's right. Everybody died. The first one died. He had a sister named Hattie. She died. Then his sister Rosa died. Then his older brother Willie died. Then Johnny died. He was the last one.
Johnny was just 48 when he died and Baby made 64.
